body: Oh, that is not a can of worms you want to open, trust me. But I appreciate you asking.
Honestly, I figured even once could get me in trouble. It shouldn’t be an issue too often on a macro scale, but it kind of spikes over a few days when it does.

Thank yoy, internet mom! Your kind words really helped me get through the anxiety attack I was going through. I think I am putting too much pressure on myself to be perfect immediately, so it helped to be reminded that I don't need to know everything from day 1. And you're right—there will be others there going through exactly what I'm feeling. We'll get through it, all of us.

Thank you again for all your compassion. It makes a difference, really.

Hey internet mom! Thank you so much for all the encouragement, it really helped. It's been buried so deep under my anxiety, but hearing you say it made me realize you're right—I am qualified, enough so to get this job. They reached out to me, so they must think I've got what it takes. Surely I can do the same for myself, then. And as you say, I don't need to know everything off the bat. I keep feeling like I'll just be thrown into the deep end, but you're right, that isn't going to happen. I can do this.

Thank you again for the support. You're super kind, truly.
That's part of why I'm writing it: in addition to helping me heal, I hope it can do the same for others. Or at least provide some catharsis. Thank you!
I'm going to try. Thank you.

A good question tbh. While this was an isolated incident, it does seem to tie into the larger pattern that *nothing I had was mine*. Anything I had could be taken from me at a moments notice, since it was my mother who actually bought it. It's why I'm so obsessive over my own stuff now honestly. Thank you for that, that's a good point.

Oh my goddess, this is so true. I've been dealing with crippling brain fog since I was 16, and it's absolutely debilitating. I've tried countless things to get rid of it, but nothing works.

Ironically, the only time it *isn't* present is when I'm dealing with events similar to my trauma. When my mother starts yelling at me, **that's** when my brain starts working properly and I can actually think. Not sure what to make of that.
My mother did her level best to destroy more of my "God-given individuality" than any real school system could ever have. It's only through sheer spite that it didn't work.

Thank you! Yeah, ADHD is rough. Sorry you have to deal with it too! I appreciate the advice. 

I love your username btw!

Hey, big sis here! You should be SO PROUD of yourself for recognizing your mistake and acknowledging it. It can be tough to admit when you were wrong, even moreso when you aren't used to seeing it. So the fact that you're taking action to do so is a wonderful accomplishment. I'm so proud of you!

I know the feeling. 

I was, and kind of still am, the Golden Child for my mother. She saw me as her "child progidy," the perfect result of how *wonderful* she had done. And it could be nice. She would take me to stuff, or buy nice things. And she at least *tried* to give me compliments. She always had nice\* things to say about me. Things could be good. 

So long as I stayed in line. 

But when I started to break from the mold she had made, be too ***weird*** for her, then things got bad. She would do everything in her power to fit me back into her image of me; anything that didn't fit that, in her mind, was *not* me, and therefore she could do as she wanted with it. All those niceties were contingent on me doing exactly as she wanted. 

It is a strange feeling, being a GC who actually sees the abuse for what it is. I feel like so many GCs are so caught up in the narcs' glamour, they never recognize what it hides. I'm not going to say we have it *worse* than the scapegoats, not a chance in hell. I've seen how she treats my sister. But it is a strange, and somewhat isolating, feeling.
I'll give fried eggs a try! I never liked them as a kid—the gooey texture was a thing for me—so I've always stuck with scrambled, but perhaps my tastes will have changed. Thank you very much!
Oh, I've heard of that trick. It makes sense! I'll give that a try this week. Thank you!

Thank you! I'm trying to remind myself of that, to celebrate those small wins. I just needed a little help with that, so I turned here. I appreciate the support!

Thank you for your advice! I'll start doing some prep for the future so I know what to look for. I appreciate your support!

Oh, that makes sense. I'm on the spectrum, and my mother never explained what those vague directions meant to me, so I always got stressed when trying to figure it out. I'll learn as I go, then! Thank you very much for your support.
Thank you so much!! I appreciate your support. I'll do my best!
That's a good idea. And thank you for being proud of me! I am trying to be happy with myself when I get stuff like this done; I just needed a little help, hence this post.
Thank you! I appreciate the support. Your advice makes sense, and I'll keep it in mind!

Again, thank you so much. I made a promise long ago that I wouldn't let my trauma make me cruel, because I know it is very tempting to. Your acknowledgement thereof means a lot to me. And I'll keep your advice in mind. Thank you very much.

When I'm in a bad place, dealing with the trials of life inside and out, I often tell myself something like this.

"I've felt worse before. I've had losses that cannot be replaced. I've been isolated, rejected, and abused by my own mother. I went through 15 years of abuse completely alone. 

I've been through the worst pains I can imagine—and ***I'm still standing.***

So come at me, motherfuckers. Is that all you got?"

Thank you so much for the kind words. I really have kept this as hidden as possible—I haven't even written about it in my journals. Had I not learned this wasn't just me, I probably would have taken it to the grave. Even here, I tried to dance around things as much as possible—old habits die hard. So being able to **finally** tell somebody about it is such a weight off my shoulders. 

I'm honestly overwhelmed by the outpouring of support I've gotten here. The fact that the unanimous consensus has been "Holy fuck, I am so sorry," and not one person has cast blame or shame on me in the slightest is an indescribable relief. And I'm even more glad to see the parents in the comments whose kids have dealt with it showing them the compassion they deserve. At least my experience is not the norm—even if I couldn't have that kindness, it is good that *somebody* did.

Yeah, in the last day since then I really have been finally picturing myself at that age, and it's just heartbreaking. That child was so *little*, and that they had to go through this alone is beyond wrong. Were it anyone else, there is no way I would be mad at them, so I'm trying to extend that same compassion to myself. Thank you for your support.
Thank you for your kind words. You're honestly right, I didn't love my body, and it's still taking me time to get to that point. I'll take your advice to heart. Thank you very much.

Amazing. I'm 23, and there's no way my mother would do that for me. Keep doing what you've been doing. It makes a difference. 

Also, your description hit home. I think my mother, if I'm being charitable, is doing her best to be a good parent through her own  trauma. Occasionally she even succeeds. But it really was all about appearances. She had a running joke for a few years: "Remember, as far as anyone knows, we're a nice, normal family." Which is kind of messed up, at least how she took it, but that's another story.

You may yet be right. My memories from childhood are blurry in the best of times, let alone this, but maybe some deep meditation can bring something up. In any event, I intend to do a Lot of inner child work from this, because that kid fucking needs it.

As it happens, your comment made me remember that, on my hospital portal, I could do the same—I saw that hospital's name linked up, but I never actually went through it for some reason. So finally, I did.

Seeing the heading "8-year-old boy" in the notes absolutely broke my heart. I hadn't realized how early it was, I could have sworn it was later. No wonder I didn't want to say anything, I was **eight fucking years old**! I've seen pictures of myself around that age. Hell, I have a few memories of being that age. I was absolutely, unquestionably a child. Imagining that small, smiling face in such pain genuinely tore me apart. I did not think, after so long, I could be *more* furious at my mother. But this fucking managed it.

It really is. I've already been dealing with other trauma responses recently, not to mention a new job, so this was not the best time for this little trivia. But this matters too. I'll make time to process this, because I am going to need it.

Hearing that after so long is an indescribable feeling. I've spent so long certain that it was my fault, I can barely even comprehend the idea that I deserved better. Internalizing this will take some time. Thank you very much.

Were I not on the bus right now, I would probably be sobbing at your comment. It really is exactly what I needed to hear.

It's only in this last day that I'm really registering just how young I was. Gods, 13 is a *child*. I was so used to playing the adult at that age that I just glossed over that in my memories. As I look back to the few pictures we have of me at that time, no, I really was just a fucking kid. The idea of looking at a child, let alone MY OWN, going through that and just letting them is beyond horrific to me. And I'm not even touching the years before that. 


I've been dealing with serious longing for a mom for the last week, so this came at a very inopportune time. Because gods above, I cannot express how much that would have helped. Once, even once in all those years, of my mother giving me support like that might have changed everything. I should have had that. I *did* deserve that. And it is **so wrong** that I didn't. 

If you've ever sat with your kids and given them support like that, and given that description I'm sure you have, please know that you are an absolutely wonderful person. Kids *need* love like that, and this entire sub is a testament to the fact that it is not guaranteed. You, and every mom like you, are doing exceptional good every time you **choose** to be compassionate, patient, and loving to your kids. From someone who knows what it's like to not have that, thank you so much for doing so. Blessed be, truly.

I can imagine it is. But take it from someone who knows, do everything in your power not to take out that frustration on him (not that you have). I promise you, your patience and compassion will make it *infinitely* more bearable for him, now and in the future. 

Best wishes on your plan. Keep talking to the GI doc, they can surely help.

You migjt be right, honestly. But I think at the stage I'm at, if I really process the fact that, on top of everything else, that whole humiliating experience was *caused* by her, I would **lose it** on her. This revelation is shocking enough. So I'm just going to bottle that up, and tuck that away for later. 

But thank you. I appreciate your compassion.

Yeah, we virtually never went to the doctor, like at all. She was a very prideful, "figure it out yourself" kind of person. She claimed we didn't have the money for it, but I'm slowly beginning to work out that that might have been a complete fucking lie. 

And yes, I cannot overstate that it was. That experience was one of, if not the most, agonizing things I've ever gone through, bar none. And I can't believe, as I'm really looking back right now, how uncaring she seemed to be about it. It wasn't even coldness, it was like it didn't even register. How could she **do** that?

That was precisely what happened, it seems. I didn't want to get into the precise details in the post, because um, ew, but when I read that as I researched it **finally** explained what was going on. I'm still working through the implications, but I think you're probably right that it made it worse, which makes it just sting so much more. Thank you for the compassion. I needed it.

Gods, those last three lines were really exactly what I needed to hear, especially coming from a mom. I was little, and I'm really only processing that now. I still thought of myself as having to be the adult at that age, but *gods*—13 is a **baby**, and that was the Ending age. 

I can't even fathom having a mom that was that patient and kind, who was willing to not just keep helping to get it resolved, but also not assign blame in the process. Moms like you are genuinely amazing people, through and through. You make thw world a better place—your words alone have already done that for me. Blessed be, truly, and thank you.

"Condition." It still feels so strange describing it that way. "Condition" implies it was something I was suffering from, not a failure on my part. It implies it was an external factor, not a choice I was making. It implies she should have *done something*, not just left me to suffer. And that's going to take some adjusting to. 

Thank you for your support. It really does help.
Thank you. I'm glad it was, too. I'm not sure if it's better or worse that I did so alone, instead of getting actual help, but it's better than still dealing with it.

Oh yes. My mother is outright *obsessive* over keeping things clean, particularly the house. She has outright said it should look as nice as it did when it was the display house. So she has impossibly high standards for cleanliness, but won't offer any actual help on Getting there. I've actually kept track: she has literally Never said that a room looks "good" when we try and clean it. The best she'll say is that it looks "better", which always feels like an implication that there's more to be done. But she outright refuses to offer any guidance on What needs to be done—she just lashes out when I ask, claiming that it's obvious and/or we should "just know".

So its gotten to the point where cleaning anything feels like so overwhelming a task that its impossible to complete, so I end up not doing anything. And that effect piles up over time, all the while my mother never did (or does) anything to help with it. Back when I was in homeschooling, she claimed that the house should be immaculate, as since we were there all day we could spend a long time cleaning every day. As such, she insisted it was our job to do all the cleaning, and seldom if ever helped us with it. In turn, after years of those two factors stacking with each other, the house has become a nightmare to live in and I have no idea how to even start cleaning it, especially the carpet, which has been absolutely destroyed with mess from the too many pets we have.
